requirements.requirement: Serve an application from node2 on TCP port 8080
requirements.summary: app8080.service (python3 http.server) deployed on node2, enabled at boot, confirmed listening on 10.50.50.2:8080 both before and after node2's restart (cmd-de4391a368434562, cmd-4c45ada7d13d4711, cmd-6748ffd3ea8a48a0).

requirements.requirement: node3 remains outside the private network shared by node1 and node2
requirements.summary: Baseline topology confirmed node3 has only the shared 10.100.56.0/24 interface (no NIC on the newly-created 10.50.50.0/24 segment). Direct attempts from node3 to the private IP and to node2's shared-network IP on 8080 both fail with 'No route to host' (cmd-1ea59829f0ab4d22, cmd-a2196f8005ec4566), confirming isolation is preserved by design (no interface added), not merely firewall-enforced.

requirements.requirement: A WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1 connects node1 and node3
requirements.summary: VyOS-native wg0 configured and committed on node1 (10.99.0.1/24, UDP 51820); node3 wg-quick@wg0 client established a live handshake with node1, confirmed again after all three restarts (cmd-5fd278ead71f4b57, cmd-622522b45bd746a7, cmd-d15f99f0b30d4db5, cmd-8d6fa679136a4192).

requirements.requirement: node3 can reach node2's app only through the WireGuard tunnel, not directly
requirements.summary: After scoping node2's firewalld to accept port 8080 only from the 10.99.0.0/24 WireGuard subnet, node3's direct curl to the private IP fails (No route to host, cmd-7703ffbf18d14f1d/cmd-e29db79e2a614a70) while curl over the tunnel (10.50.50.2:8080 routed via wg0) succeeds with HTTP 200 (cmd-7e21cd83c5444edd). Direct access to node2's shared-network IP is also blocked (cmd-a2196f8005ec4566). Verified again post-restart (cmd-ae4452a782994812, cmd-1a76cd3a1a7b4910, cmd-8d6fa679136a4192).

requirements.requirement: Independent node-restart evidence protocol: node1 pre/post restart with recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id 4098161f..., wg0/eth1 state, cmd-3adc6cef1d33445f), restart acknowledged (cmd-dce49f9fedd04022), connection loss observed during the bounded window (cmd-01f5efa644e14c35, cmd-eae785fa0764417b), new boot_id 5cd424be... confirmed (cmd-bac876d605564c3d, cross-checked against global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity), and full recovery of eth1/wg0 addressing, wg peer config, IP forwarding, and end-to-end tunnel reachability (cmd-d15f99f0b30d4db5, cmd-1a76cd3a1a7b4910).

requirements.requirement: Independent node-restart evidence protocol: node2 pre/post restart with recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline (boot_id be303eb3..., app active, cmd-22e91191dbf1489f), restart ack (cmd-82a2099489c443b8), connection loss observed (cmd-6325f94336834a69), new boot_id 809cf3b0... confirmed, and full recovery of the app service, private IP, static route, and firewalld rich rule (cmd-6748ffd3ea8a48a0), plus tunnel-path reachability re-verified from node3 (cmd-ae4452a782994812).

requirements.requirement: Independent node-restart evidence protocol: node3 pre/post restart with recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline (boot_id 21de1f79..., wg-quick active, cmd-24ee47ddabb544f4), restart ack (cmd-cdf9ae951a0d4d69), connection loss observed (cmd-1c92bab7fc504bb9, cmd-c6d04a25eb7745ae, cmd-b0e699fab96b4285), new boot_id ca04a675... confirmed, and full recovery of the wg-quick service with fresh handshake and successful app fetch over the tunnel (cmd-8d6fa679136a4192).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct evidence: node2 serves the app on 8080, node3 stays outside the node1/node2 private segment, a WireGuard tunnel terminates on node1 and connects to node3, and node3 can reach the app only through that tunnel (verified by contrasting failed direct attempts with a successful tunneled HTTP 200). The independently-required node-restart evidence protocol was executed cleanly on all three nodes with coherent pre-restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full recovery of network, service, and tunnel state, cross-checked against the fixed after-executor snapshots. The only notable operational-hygiene issue is a bounded, self-terminating diagnostic tcpdump capture on node1 that did not contribute to the eventual fix, though it left no persistent residue after node1's reboot.
limitations: The tcpdump capture output (/tmp/wg0.pcap.txt, /tmp/eth1.pcap.txt) was never shown being read in the trace, so its role (if any) in diagnosis cannot be fully ruled out beyond what is visible.
No prepare phase was configured (prepare_enabled=false, after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on before/after-executor comparison.

operational_hygiene.summary: One unnecessary mutation identified: a background tcpdump packet capture on node1 (cmd-f877e06ca88a411f) launched during troubleshooting of the firewalld block, writing to /tmp/wg0.pcap.txt and /tmp/eth1.pcap.txt. The trace shows the actual root cause (firewalld REJECT) was diagnosed and fixed directly via firewall-cmd inspection (cmd-93859b5828f74cfb) without evidence the tcpdump output was ever used, so this capture had no clear causal role in the fix. It was bounded (count-limited to 10 packets, self-terminating) and low-risk, and any residue was implicitly cleared by node1's later reboot (/tmp is not present in the post-restart temporary-files inventory). All other state-changing commands (interface addressing, app service creation, WireGuard key/config setup, static route, firewalld rich rule) map directly to satisfying task requirements. No failed services, no damaged package state, and no retained unsafe exposure were observed in the after-executor snapshot.
